Among all differentials, MMN best fits the *triad*: (1) progressive asymmetric upper limb motor weakness, (2) no sensory involvement, (3) subacute course — and it is the *only condition in the list that is both immune-mediated and specifically associated with anti-GM1 antibodies and NCS-documented conduction block*. While flail arm ALS can mimic this, it lacks serological biomarkers, shows chronic neurogenic changes on EMG (not acute denervation alone), and has no effective disease-modifying therapy — whereas MMN is treatable and must be ruled out *first* to avoid misdiagnosis and delay of IVIG. All other tests ordered are consistent with MMN evaluation — including excluding mimics (e.g., myasthenia via anti-MuSK/AChR, paraneoplastic via CSF, metabolic causes via B12/thyroid).
